scope: Round 6 native supervisor EOF shutdown finding only
changes: The launcher observes POLLHUP/POLLRDHUP independently of its bounded input selector registration, including an 8 MiB saturated bridge with unread kernel bytes.
The two-second streaming shutdown deadline begins on actual upstream closure or observed EOF and is never reset by deferred child-stdin closure. Pending bytes may drain during that grace period.
NativeRpc destroys launcher stdin only after fail() classifies sent work as unknown and queued work as not_sent, so a buffered write cannot prevent EOF from reaching the launcher.
The existing clean_children descendant verification and nonzero cleanup-failure acknowledgement remain mandatory; no UID, sudo, environment, signal permission or inherited-descriptor policy changed.

Real Linux pipe and socket half-close tests cover buffered EOF, full bridge/kernel buffers, detached descendants and unconfirmed cleanup; runtime integration covers the actual Node socket to Python bridge to non-reading child and idempotent write-error failure handling.
The large-frame hash regression now pauses its consumer for three seconds while the upstream remains open, proving ordinary backpressure does not start the two-second closure deadline.
